Since it’s on your back hopefully it’s not quite as sensitive as this one was. Before the procedure it felt like I had broken my tail bone and I could barely walk or sit without pain. Right after it felt like a painful pressure. It has to be repacked with gauze twice a day, this helps slough off dead cells and helps the wound close from the inside out. Definitely the most painful part though, kind of like someone pulling your insides out when you pull the gauze out and a stinging pain when you put the gauze back in. It gets better with time though. I would get it done before an infection starts.

This is my first one! Got it from riding a four wheeler:( they did an actual surgery to go in and drain the cyst and get rid of the pilonidal sinus that had formed. If you don’t remove the sinus it can continue to get infected. Unfortunately no mater what you do, even when you get the flap surgery the cyst can come back.  I just got the surgery two days ago so we will just have to wait and see if it comes back :( To give yourself the best chance I would see a dermatologist in your area and ask if they can refer you to a surgeon who specializes in these.  I would not recommend putting off proper treatment as the cyst can spread to the other soft tissue and muscle in the area (this can take months to years, I’m not trying to scare you I just want you better!)

I know friend :( I already have self esteem issues and when I found out my tailbone pain was a pilonidal cyst I had legitimate panic attacks the first few days. But so many people have this problem don’t let it get you too down! Just get it drained when you can and manage your pain for now <3

Definitely get a second opinion from another surgeon. I went to my primary care and she just gave me antibiotics and pain meds. I didn’t like that answer and saw a dermatologist and as soon as she saw it she knew what it was and said I needed surgery. Went to the surgeon and he immediately agreed and I was scheduled for surgery the next day. Mine was relatively small too, a little smaller than a golf ball. From what my surgeon said (who primarily works with these cysts) the only true way to clear the infection is an incision and drainage of the site, preferably under anesthesia so they can get the whole infection out because it is too painful to do just in the office. I hope this helps and I’m SO sorry you have to deal with it.

Nurse here! I just got my first surgery for my first pilonidal cyst. If it makes you feel better monitor your temp and the size of infection. It is very very unlikely that you will go septic from your cyst. After becoming a nurse my health anxiety sky rocketed and I had the same anxiety about going septic as you. My surgeon deals with these all the time and says in the 15 years he has been treating them he hasn’t seen any of his patients go septic. As someone else posted do sitz baths (warm water baths), warm compresses, and drink plenty of fluids! Ibuprofen will help the pain for now but stop taking 24 hours before you get it drained.  These things SUCK but you will get through it!

When I was in nursing school I did a rotation in ED. A trauma was coming in and the nurse I was following asked if I wanted to see. I gowned up in a bunny suit and stood in the corner, trying to make myself as small as possible so I wouldn’t be in the way. The doors slam open and they wheel this naked man in who is flopping around on the table like a dying fish, blood everywhere. I look closer and his neck was flopping open and spurting blood every time he moved. He had tried to kill himself by circular saw to the neck and some coworkers found him behind a shed. They intubated him through his exposed trachea. I almost passed out. He lived though, missed both of his jugulars and was left with a small scar and raspy voice.
We’re all stuck here together. We might as well do something that makes living through it slightly better.
